data.description:
## The finding

Three `rebar/host` metrics have published **ZERO datapoints in 7+ days**:

- `disk_used_percent` with `mount=/var/gerrit`
- `gerrit_healthy`
- `reviewbot_healthy`

Any alarm fed by these is **currently unfalsifiable**: it cannot go to ALARM for a real condition
because no data ever arrives, and with `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` it either sits
permanently breaching or its state reflects nothing at all. Either way the alarm has stopped being
a measurement.

## How it was found, and the trap that hides it

During tonight's outage recovery I needed to verify that `/var/gerrit` had actually remounted —
important because `user_data.sh` asserts the gate-scratch mount but NOT `/var/gerrit`, both fstab
entries use `nofail`, and `mount -a` returns 0 while silently skipping (bug
`unamused-cloudy-junebug`). The natural check is `disk_used_percent{mount=/var/gerrit}`.

**The signal bug `unamused-cloudy-junebug` calls for does not exist to be read.** It has been dead
for a week.

**THE TRAP, which is the important part of this ticket:** these metric names still appear in
`cloudwatch list-metrics`. That only proves they published at some point within roughly the last
two weeks — CloudWatch retains the metric NAME long after datapoints stop. So a reader checking
"does this metric exist?" gets YES for a metric that has been silent for seven days. Verifying a
metric requires querying its DATAPOINTS over a window, not listing its name.

That is why this went unnoticed: every superficial check says the telemetry is present.

## Why this is its own ticket

It is adjacent to but distinct from the tickets already open:

- `fab-dismal-haddock` is about the absence of off-box LOGS and the inability to diagnose an
  outage after the fact. This is about METRICS that appear configured and are silently dead.
- `herbal-garish-monkey` fixed `treat_missing_data` inversions so a dead publisher would PAGE.
  That work is correct and it caught tonight's outage in seven minutes. But it assumed the
  publisher publishes when healthy; a publisher that stopped a week ago is a different state, and
  these three slipped through.
- `unamused-cloudy-junebug` needs an assertion that `/var/gerrit` is mounted. This ticket explains
  why the obvious implementation of that assertion would silently do nothing today.

## Consequence during tonight's incident

`/var/gerrit` could NOT be verified as mounted from off-box. The best available substitute was EBS
I/O discrimination — the data volume showed 49,834 reads in the boot window against 49 on the
newly-attached raw scratch volume, three orders of magnitude apart, so it is almost certainly
mounted and serving. **That is an inference from I/O, not a mount check.** A definitive answer
needs a read-only on-box `findmnt /var/gerrit`.

An outage in which the operator cannot confirm the primary data volume is mounted is the concrete
cost of this defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - Determine WHY each of the three stopped publishing, and fix it. They may share one
      cause or have three; say which. A fix that restores publishing without explaining the stop
      leaves the recurrence path open.
- [ ] AC2 - A metric that STOPS publishing is detected as such, distinctly from "the metric is
      reporting a bad value" and distinctly from "the metric name is absent". Prove it by stopping
      a publisher and observing the detection.
- [ ] AC3 - The check does NOT rely on `list-metrics` name presence, which returns YES for metrics
      silent for days. It must assert on datapoint recency over a defined window.
- [ ] AC4 - An audit exists of ALL `rebar/host` metrics establishing which are live, so this class
      is enumerated rather than discovered one at a time during an incident. Record the audit
      result in the tree.
- [ ] AC5 - Defect-seeded: the detection itself fails loudly if IT stops running. A liveness check
      that silently dies reproduces the exact defect one level up — the same
      absence-of-execution-reported-as-success class recurring throughout this repo.

## Non-goals

Not adding the `/var/gerrit` mount assertion (that is `unamused-cloudy-junebug`). Not off-box log
shipping (that is `fab-dismal-haddock`). Not re-auditing `treat_missing_data` (that is
`herbal-garish-monkey`).
data.title: Three rebar/host metrics have published nothing for 7+ days, making their alarms unfalsifiable — and list-metrics still shows the names, so every superficial check says the telemetry is fine
